summary: Screw-pile light on a Chesapeake Bay shoal, first lit 1889. Its head keeper died in 1931 under disputed circumstances; automated on the same foundation from 1960.

structures.note: Hexagonal wooden house on a screw-pile foundation; taken down in 1960
Automated light on the original screw-pile foundation

access.note: Not open to the public (US Lighthouse Society archive). Accessible only by boat (Chesapeake Chapter).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says a modern light is still shown from the screw-pile foundation. The 'inactive' value may reflect the 1960 end of the manned station; for human review. The USLHS record also says 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No', so the archive and LighthouseFriends disagree; the proposed value is not settled. The 2025 Light List entry (LLNR 7545) agrees, but the navcen PDF could not be read by the checker.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1960 'deactivated' belongs to the manned station, which ended in 1960. The archive and LighthouseFriends say an automated light went onto the same foundation that year, so the light itself continued.
The record's 1960 first year (Wikidata) belongs to the replacement tower; 1889 is the original station.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28: (1) The Chesapeake Chapter keeper timeline differs from the USLHS roster: Henry R. Hanberry 'at least 1939 - 1943' (USLHS 1938-1940), Ulysses S. Todd '1931 -' (USLHS 1931-1938), Henry T. McGrath '1911 - at least 1913' (USLHS 1911-1914), Wilbur S. Kelly 'at least 1919 - 1925' (USLHS 1918-1925). The story uses the USLHS dates only and states none of these. (2) The 1918 Lighthouse Service Bulletin index lists a 'McDorman, William F., asst keeper Great Shoals, rescue' and 'McDorman, W.F., keeper Great Shoals, rescue'; the story does not link them to the Holland Island Bar McDorman, and no source in hand does. (3) The archive's 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No' conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 'modern light is shown'; the story states both. (4) Evening Star p. 5 and Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1918 PDF page 20 were confirmed in the cache and corpus. Owens death date: LighthouseFriends gives 15 March 1931, a Sunday. The Chesapeake Bay Magazine article begins on the night of 11 March 1931, when the light was dark (a Wednesday). The Evening Star (20 March 1931) gives weekdays only: the light was out on Saturday night, the body was found on Sunday afternoon and buried on Wednesday. Those weekdays fit LighthouseFriends' Sunday 15 March and not the magazine's 11 March, so the story says the sources disagree on the date and does not pick one. Wikipedia's lead gives 31 March 1931 and was not used. 1957: LighthouseFriends says four men were evacuated; the Chesapeake Chapter says two keepers were injured; the magazine says no one was hurt. No Chronicling America page for 1957 was found (searches for 'Holland Island Bar' with Navy, 'Crisfield' with Skyraiders, and 'Holland' with lighthouse and rockets returned nothing). The 1888 appropriation, the 1889 scow and the 1889-90 construction come from LighthouseFriends quoting the Light-House Board reports. The corpus holds Light-House Board volumes only for 1891-1901; the 1899 entry was checked at scan page 141, and the 1888-1890 reports are cited as LighthouseFriends quotes them, not checked against the primary volumes. The Coast Guard Historian's Holland Island Bar page was not readable: the Wayback captures returned an index or a 404. Focal height: the archive gives 42 ft above water for the 1889 house; the record's ENC figure is 11.3 m; the Light List height column reads 15 with no unit in the cached text. Not used in the facts. Record status 'inactive' conflicts with the 2025 Light List (see corrections). The Light List Volume II (2025) entry for LLNR 7545 reads Fl W 2.5s, range 6 nm, skeleton tower on piles; it matches the record's ENC values. The navcen PDF (LightList_V2_2025.pdf) returned HTTP 403 to the checker, so the Light List is not cited in the story or the evidence. The local copy is at data/raw/uscg_light_list/LightList_V2_2025.pdf. The characteristic and range are left out of facts for that reason. County: the record says Somerset. Wikipedia's Holland Island article (lead only) places the island in Dorchester County. The light's county was not verified, so the prose gives no county. Fog signal: the record has none. LighthouseFriends gives a machine-struck bell for 1889-90; the current signal is not in the cached Light List line. Owner: no source named one; the record says unknown. The Wikipedia lead gives a 10-second flash and 12-mile range; the Light List gives Fl W 2.5s and 6 nm, and the Light List was used. The Commissioner of Lighthouses 1918 listing of McDorman (OCR 'McDonnan') was not used. Roster: 47 lines from the USLHS archive, which takes them from the NARA keeper registers (via the Kraig Anderson inventory). Not checked against primary registers. Edward R. Somers and Edgar T. Somers share a surname; no link is stated, and none is inferred.
